description: Triage of the CyberChef default sweep. Every comparable operation was run in upstream CyberChef and in rx-chef against the same input under each side's own argument defaults. Every entry states a checkable reason; no entry may read 'unknown'.

reference_provenance.note: No operation source was modified in the capture checkout, which the capture tool verifies and refuses to proceed otherwise. The listed paths are a lockfile and local scratch files unrelated to operation behaviour.

entries.reason: The upstream keyword argument was not reproduced by the sweep's default resolution, so rx-chef ran with an empty keyword while upstream used its own.

Upstream treats the input as the raw secret; rx-chef base32-encodes it before building the otpauth URI. Needs a decision on which reading is intended.
Upstream emits the full CRC catalogue; rx-chef emits a different, smaller set. Not an argument problem alone — the operations enumerate different algorithm lists.

entries.reason: Sliced its hex input as a &str by byte offset; non-ASCII input becomes three-byte U+FFFD characters, so the length stayed even while the slice landed inside a character and panicked. Only reachable with --features disassembly.

Reported a SHA-1 digest under the 'SHA0' label (the source comment read "using SHA1 as proxy"). SHA-0 and SHA-1 differ by a rotate in the message schedule, so the published value was simply wrong. Now uses the real SHA-0.
Same defect as Chi Square: raw IEEE-754 bytes instead of decimal text.

entries.reason: Implemented only the Standard format (the bit packer hardcoded 16 bits per character) and iterated Unicode scalar values instead of UTF-16 code units, truncating astral characters and making upstream streams undecodable. All four formats now work and non-BMP input is byte-identical with upstream.
The serialized byte length was used to slice a &str and panicked when it fell inside a multi-byte character; four 0xFF bytes reached it.

Its alphabet expansion was a literal substring replacement, so it rejected the URL-safe alphabet that From Base64 accepts and upstream supports, and it padded unconditionally regardless of whether the alphabet declares a padding character. All Base-N operations now share src/alphabet.rs.
Emitted one space between the hex and ASCII columns; hexdump -C and upstream use two, so every line was a character narrow.
